title: Given an unsorted array of numbers and a value K, find the Kth smallest number. Explain how a max-heap of size K keeps the K smallest seen so far, with its root being the answer.
shortTitle: Kth Smallest Number (Find the Kth Smallest with a Max-Heap)
keyPoints: Keep a max-heap of size K holding the K smallest numbers; its root is the Kth smallest
In Java, use PriorityQueue with Collections.reverseOrder() for a max-heap
Seed the heap with the first K elements, then for each remaining element replace root only if smaller
Time complexity is O(n log K), space is O(K), which beats full sorting at O(n log n)
For a single query on a static array, quickselect gives O(n) average time as an alternative
This is the inverse of Kth Largest: Kth smallest uses a max-heap, Kth largest uses a min-heap
Works on streaming data where you cannot sort the entire dataset upfront

s1_definition.oneliner: Keep a max-heap of size K of the smallest numbers seen so far; its root is the Kth smallest.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Kth Smallest** – find the element that would be at index K - 1 if the array were fully sorted in ascending order.
- **Max-heap of size K** – holds the K smallest numbers seen so far; its root is the largest of those K, which is exactly the Kth smallest overall.
- **Insertion rule** – if a new number is smaller than the root, evict the root and insert the new number; otherwise discard it.
- **Complexity** – O(n log K) time and O(K) space, better than O(n log n) sorting when K is much smaller than n.
- **Alternative** – quickselect gives average O(n) for a single query on a static in-memory array.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, Priya wants to find the Kth cheapest fee among thousands of fees charged across all branches. She keeps a small bucket holding only the K smallest fees seen so far, with the biggest fee in that bucket sitting on top. Each new fee is compared against that top: if it is smaller, it replaces the top; otherwise it is discarded. After scanning all fees, the top of the bucket is the Kth smallest fee.

sections.s6_takeaway:
The Kth Smallest Number problem is a Top K Elements problem where the heap choice is the counter-intuitive part. To find the Kth smallest, you keep a max-heap of size K. The heap holds the K smallest numbers seen so far, and because it is a max-heap its root is the largest of those K, which once all numbers are processed is precisely the Kth smallest overall.

You seed the heap with elements and evict the root whenever the heap exceeds size K. A number larger than the root can never be among the K smallest, so it gets discarded after the eviction. The root being the largest kept value is what makes the keep-or-discard test a single peek, and it is also why the root is the answer at the end.

At the National Bank of India, Priya used this for a fairness audit that needed the Kth smallest fee among thousands charged across branches, without sorting every fee. A size-K max-heap of the smallest fees let each new fee displace the largest kept fee only if it was smaller, giving the answer in O(n log K) time.

A senior engineer also mentions quickselect as an average O(n) alternative for a single query on a static array, which shows the interviewer you know when the heap is the right tool and when it is not. The heap wins on streaming data where elements arrive over time and you cannot wait to sort.

Remember one sentence: for the Kth smallest, use a max-heap of size K and the root is your answer.
